name: webhook-delivery-service
goals: Clients read and write domain resources over HTTP.
Customers or operators manage resources through an authenticated API.
Producers hand events to the system, which persists them before acknowledging.
Work is queued durably and performed by workers with a retry schedule.
Events are delivered to endpoints customers registered.
Outbound requests carry an HMAC signature; secrets rotate with a grace window.
The system notifies people through an external channel.
Targets that keep failing are disabled by policy and the owner is told.
Metrics, structured logs and health endpoints for operations.
Scheduled jobs process stored records in windows.
Changes are recorded append-only with the actor.

rules: Type hints on every public function; dataclasses or pydantic for records.
No business logic in the HTTP layer.
Every management route goes through the authentication middleware; no route is exempt without a decision.
Every component logs one structured line per unit of work with the correlation id.
No in-process state that a second instance would not see; instances are interchangeable.
Prefer the boring option; a new piece of infrastructure needs a decision record.
Python 3.12 as stated in the constraints.
Stateless processes: configuration from the environment, no local files that a second instance would not see.
definition_of_done: Acceptance checks of the package pass.
No file outside the write scope changed.
Every public operation of the implemented interfaces exists with the declared inputs.

requirements.statement: Customers register webhook endpoints; when things happen in our platform (order.created, order.paid, refund.issued, ...) we must deliver a signed JSON event to every endpoint subscribed to that event type.
Customers manage endpoints via an admin HTTP API: create/list/delete endpoints, choose event types, rotate the signing secret.
Internal services publish events through an internal API (HTTP or in-process call).

Each event is delivered at least once to every matching endpoint. Deliveries are retried with exponential backoff (1 min, 5 min, 30 min, 2 h, 12 h; 5 attempts) on 5xx/timeout. 4xx (except 429) is final failure. 429 honours Retry-After.
Every delivery carries an HMAC-SHA256 signature over the body with the endpoint's current secret, plus a timestamp header; after rotation, both old and new secrets are valid for 24 h.
Customers can see delivery attempts per event (status, response code, timestamps) and manually redeliver.
Endpoints that fail continuously for 3 days are disabled automatically and the customer is notified by email.
1,000 events/s sustained publish rate, 5,000 endpoints; delivery latency p95 under 5 s for a healthy endpoint.
No event lost on process crash (persist before ack).

metric.name: records lost across a process crash

requirements.statement: Per-endpoint isolation: one slow endpoint must not delay others.

metric.name: p95 latency of healthy targets while one target stalls

requirements.statement: metrics (queue depth, delivery success rate, attempt latency) exposed for Prometheus; structured logs.
Python 3.12, PostgreSQL available, Redis available. Single region. Team of 3.
Must run as a set of stateless containers behind our existing ingress.
Domain records are kept indefinitely; logs and audit history are retained for 1 year, after which a nightly job deletes them (assumed by the engine).

components.name: Customer endpoint
components.responsibility: The customer's HTTPS receiver; outside our control.

components.name: Audit log
components.responsibility: Append-only record of who did what to which resource, queryable by resource and actor.

components.name: Domain core
components.responsibility: Business rules and validation for the domain entities; the only module that changes state through the store.

components.name: Outbound HTTP client
components.responsibility: Performs the outbound HTTP call with timeouts, size limits, redirect and private-address protection, and returns a classified outcome.

components.name: Signer
components.responsibility: Produces and verifies HMAC signatures over request bodies with the current and previous secrets.

components.name: Notifier
components.responsibility: Sends operator/customer notifications through the configured channel with templating and rate limiting.

components.name: Observability
components.responsibility: Metrics registry and exposition, structured logging, health/readiness endpoints.

components.name: Authentication
components.responsibility: Authenticates callers and resolves them to a principal and scope; enforces authorization for management operations.

components.name: Worker
components.responsibility: Leases work items, performs the outbound action, records the outcome, and decides retry vs. final failure.

components.name: Scheduler
components.responsibility: Computes when deferred work runs next (backoff schedules, periodic jobs) and promotes due work.

components.name: Health policy
components.responsibility: Evaluates per-target failure history against the disable policy and applies the consequence.

components.name: Batch job
components.responsibility: Scheduled processing over stored records: extract, transform, aggregate, write results.

components.name: Admin HTTP API
components.responsibility: Management surface for operators/customers: resource lifecycle and configuration; authenticated.

components.name: Ingest API
components.responsibility: Accepts events/records from producers, validates them, persists them, and enqueues work; acknowledges only after persistence.

components.name: Event domain
components.responsibility: Owns the Event aggregate: creation, changes and state transitions of these records, and the rules that hold across them. Event states: delivered, published; transitions not stated. Read from R-1, R-3, R-4, R-6.

decisions.title: API style
decisions.context: Clients need a programmable surface.

options.name: GraphQL
cons: complexity budget for a small team

decisions.rationale: Scored against the active qualities; decided by durability (weight 1.0), performance (weight 0.82). REST/JSON over HTTP: 2.37; gRPC: 1.25; GraphQL: 1.12. stated in the constraints
decisions.consequences: Not choosing 'gRPC' gives up: typed contracts, streaming. Not choosing 'GraphQL' gives up: flexible queries.

decisions.title: Primary store
decisions.context: Domain records need durable, queryable storage.

options.name: MySQL / MariaDB (the stated database)
cons: weaker JSON and DDL ergonomics than PostgreSQL

options.name: Redis for the hot state (as stated) with a relational store for durable records
pros: the stated home of the hot data

options.name: Managed document store (DynamoDB/MongoDB, as stated)
cons: query patterns must be designed up front

decisions.rationale: Scored against the active qualities; decided by durability (weight 1.0), performance (weight 0.82). PostgreSQL: 3.27; MySQL / MariaDB: unavailable (needs mysql, not in the constraints); Redis for the hot state: unavailable (needs redis_primary, not in the constraints); Managed document store: unavailable (needs document_db, not in the constraints); SQLite: unavailable (ruled out by containers, multi_instance); Files: unavailable (ruled out by containers, multi_instance); In-memory: unavailable (ruled out by containers, multi_instance, postgres, durable_required). stated in the constraints

decisions.title: Caller authentication
decisions.context: Management operations must be attributable to a customer or operator.

options.name: API keys per customer, hashed at rest, sent as a bearer token
cons: no delegation or expiry unless added

options.name: OAuth2 / OIDC with the platform's identity provider
Session tokens issued by the platform's own account service to game/mobile clients (device-bound, short-lived, refreshable)
No account: a reference number plus a knowledge factor (date of birth) resumes a saved application; every attempt rate-limited and logged
pros: no credentials to manage for occasional users
cons: a reference number can be shared; scope what it unlocks

options.name: Email one-time code / magic link (no account needed)

decisions.choice: API keys per customer, hashed at rest, sent as a bearer token
decisions.rationale: Scored against the active qualities; decided by durability (weight 1.0), performance (weight 0.82). API keys per customer, hashed at rest, sent as a: 1.33; Mutual TLS: 1.04; OAuth2 / OIDC with the platform's identity provi: unavailable (needs idp, not in the constraints); Session tokens issued by the platform's own acco: unavailable (needs game_client, not in the constraints); No account: a reference number plus a knowledge : unavailable (needs no_account_auth, not in the constraints); Email one-time code / magic link: unavailable (needs email_auth, not in the constraints). chosen in the interview
decisions.consequences: Not choosing 'Mutual TLS' gives up: strong, no secrets in headers.

decisions.title: How producers publish
decisions.context: Internal services must hand events to the system.

options.name: HTTP publish endpoint with idempotency keys
In-process client library that writes the outbox in the caller's transaction
pros: no lost events at the source
cons: couples callers to our schema and language

decisions.choice: HTTP publish endpoint with idempotency keys
decisions.rationale: Scored against the active qualities; decided by durability (weight 1.0), performance (weight 0.82). HTTP publish endpoint with idempotency keys: 1.79; In-process client library that writes the outbox: 1.56; Message bus topic: unavailable (needs broker, not in the constraints)
decisions.consequences: Not choosing 'In-process client library that writes the outbox' gives up: no lost events at the source.

decisions.title: Work queue technology
decisions.context: Work items must survive a crash and be leased by several workers.

options.name: PostgreSQL table with SELECT ... FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED
pros: transactional with the domain data (persist + enqueue atomically)
cons: throughput bounded by the database (fine to ~10k items/s)

options.name: Redis Streams with consumer groups
pros: built-in consumer groups and pending lists
cons: separate from the transactional store: needs an outbox

options.name: Managed broker (SQS/RabbitMQ/Kafka)
cons: at-least-once semantics still need an outbox

decisions.choice: PostgreSQL table with SELECT ... FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED
decisions.rationale: Scored against the active qualities; decided by durability (weight 1.0), performance (weight 0.82). PostgreSQL table with SELECT ... FOR UPDATE SKIP: 3.13; Redis Streams with consumer groups: 1.81; Managed broker: unavailable (needs broker, not in the constraints); In-memory queue: unavailable (ruled out by durable_required, containers, multi_instance). stated in the constraints
decisions.consequences: Not choosing 'Redis Streams with consumer groups' gives up: high throughput, built-in consumer groups and pending lists.

decisions.title: Where delayed retries wait
decisions.context: Failed deliveries must run again at a computed future time.

options.name: not_before column on the work item; the scheduler promotes due rows
pros: one durable store for queued and delayed items
trivial to inspect and to redeliver manually

options.name: Redis sorted set keyed by due time
cons: a second store to keep consistent

decisions.choice: not_before column on the work item; the scheduler promotes due rows
decisions.rationale: Scored against the active qualities; decided by durability (weight 1.0), performance (weight 0.82). not_before column on the work item: 1.91; Redis sorted set keyed by due time: 1.49; In-process timers: unavailable (ruled out by durable_required, containers, multi_instance)
decisions.consequences: Not choosing 'Redis sorted set keyed by due time' gives up: cheap due-time queries.

decisions.title: Process topology
decisions.context: The same code base serves requests and performs background work.

options.name: One image, role by flag: `api` and `worker` processes scale independently
pros: independent scaling of ingress and outbound work

options.name: Single process with background threads
cons: request latency competes with outbound work

options.name: Separate services per concern (ingest, admin, delivery)
cons: three deployables for a team of three

decisions.choice: One image, role by flag: `api` and `worker` processes scale independently
decisions.rationale: Scored against the active qualities; decided by durability (weight 1.0), performance (weight 0.82). One image, role by flag: `api` and `worker` proc: 1.87; Separate services per concern: 1.64; Single process with background threads: 1.36
decisions.consequences: Not choosing 'Separate services per concern' gives up: clear ownership. Not choosing 'Single process with background threads' gives up: one deployable.

decisions.title: Outbound request safety
decisions.context: The system makes HTTP requests to customer-supplied URLs.

options.name: Resolve and block private/link-local ranges; pin the resolved IP; cap body size and redirects; per-request timeout
Plain HTTP client with a timeout

decisions.choice: Resolve and block private/link-local ranges; pin the resolved IP; cap body size and redirects; per-request timeout
decisions.rationale: Scored against the active qualities; decided by durability (weight 1.0), performance (weight 0.82). Resolve and block private/link-local ranges: 1.41; Plain HTTP client with a timeout: 1.16
decisions.consequences: Not choosing 'Plain HTTP client with a timeout' gives up: simplest.

decisions.title: Storage of signing secrets
decisions.context: Per-endpoint secrets are sensitive and must be readable by workers.

options.name: Encrypted column (AES-GCM) with a key from the environment/KMS
External secrets manager (Vault/KMS-backed)
cons: latency and a new dependency on the hot path

options.name: Plaintext column
cons: database dump exposes every customer secret

decisions.choice: Encrypted column (AES-GCM) with a key from the environment/KMS
decisions.rationale: Scored against the active qualities; decided by durability (weight 1.0), performance (weight 0.82). Encrypted column: 1.53; Plaintext column: 1.31; External secrets manager: unavailable (needs vault, not in the constraints)
decisions.consequences: Not choosing 'Plaintext column' gives up: simplest.

decisions.title: Per-target isolation of outbound work
decisions.context: One slow or failing target must not delay work for the others.

options.name: Partition the queue by target; each lease takes one partition with a per-partition concurrency cap
pros: a slow target only occupies its own slot

options.name: Single FIFO queue with a global worker pool
cons: one slow target blocks pool slots for everyone (head-of-line blocking)

options.name: Hash targets to N shards, one worker pool per shard
pros: bounded blast radius without per-target state
cons: a slow target still delays its shard

decisions.choice: Partition the queue by target; each lease takes one partition with a per-partition concurrency cap
decisions.rationale: Scored against the active qualities; decided by durability (weight 1.0), performance (weight 0.82). Partition the queue by target: 1.76; Hash targets to N shards, one worker pool per sh: 1.56; Single FIFO queue with a global worker pool: 1.34
decisions.consequences: Not choosing 'Hash targets to N shards, one worker pool per sh' gives up: bounded blast radius without per-target state. Not choosing 'Single FIFO queue with a global worker pool' gives up: simplest.

decisions.title: Redundancy for the availability target
decisions.context: The availability target must be met through instance failures and deploys.

options.name: Two or more interchangeable instances per role behind the ingress, health checks, rolling deploys
cons: needs stateless instances and a shared store

decisions.choice: Two or more interchangeable instances per role behind the ingress, health checks, rolling deploys
decisions.rationale: Scored against the active qualities; decided by durability (weight 1.0), performance (weight 0.82). Two or more interchangeable instances per role b: 1.51; Single instance with health-based restart: 1.24; Active-active across two regions: unavailable (ruled out by single_region)
decisions.consequences: Not choosing 'Single instance with health-based restart' gives up: simplest, cheapest.

risks.description: Payloads or uploads without size limits exhaust memory or disk.
risks.mitigation: Enforce size limits at the surface; reject early with a clear error.

risks.description: Entities evolve; migrations run against live data.
risks.mitigation: Versioned migrations applied before deploy; additive changes first, removals one release later.

risks.description: A management operation reachable without authentication.
risks.mitigation: Authenticate in one middleware for every management route; test every route unauthenticated.

risks.description: At-least-once delivery means a target can receive the same event twice (crash between call and ack).
risks.mitigation: Send a stable event id and attempt number in headers; document idempotent consumption; never retry on 2xx.

risks.description: Many targets fail at once (regional outage) and their retries align, creating a burst.
risks.mitigation: Add jitter to the backoff schedule and cap concurrent deliveries per partition and globally.

risks.description: Customer-supplied URLs can point at internal addresses or metadata services.
risks.mitigation: Resolve before connecting, block private ranges, pin the IP, forbid redirects to non-public hosts.

risks.description: Retried and dead-lettered items accumulate and slow the lease query.
risks.mitigation: Partial index on (partition, not_before) for live items; archive terminal items on a schedule.

risks.description: Timestamp-based signatures and not_before scheduling depend on wall clocks.
risks.mitigation: Use the database clock for scheduling; tolerate a bounded skew window when verifying timestamps.

risks.description: Signing secrets in the database are exposed by a dump or a read-only breach.
risks.mitigation: Encrypt at rest with a key outside the database; log secret reads; rotate on suspicion.

risks.description: A widespread failure disables many targets and emails every owner at once.
risks.mitigation: Rate-limit notifications per owner and batch them.

risks.description: Per-target labels on metrics explode cardinality.
risks.mitigation: Label by outcome and partition class, not by target id; expose per-target detail through the API instead.

risks.description: [tampering] Store: Injection through query construction.
risks.mitigation: Parameterised queries only; no string-built SQL. Check: static check for string-formatted SQL finds nothing

risks.description: [information_disclosure] Store: Backups and dumps contain everything.
risks.mitigation: Encrypt backups; restrict who can take them. Check: backup file is not readable without the key

risks.description: [denial_of_service] Work queue: A poison item is retried forever and blocks its partition.
risks.mitigation: Attempt cap and dead-letter; per-partition concurrency cap. Check: an always-failing item ends in the dead-letter after the cap

risks.description: [tampering] Work queue: Items are processed twice after a crash between call and ack.
risks.mitigation: Idempotent processing with the item id; ack only after the outcome is recorded. Check: kill the worker mid-call; the item is redelivered exactly once more

risks.description: [information_disclosure] Secret store: Secrets readable from a database dump or a read-only breach.
risks.mitigation: Encrypt at rest with a key held outside the database; never log values. Check: database dump contains no plaintext secret; grep logs for secret prefixes finds nothing

risks.description: [elevation] Secret store: A rotated secret stays valid forever.
risks.mitigation: Bound the grace window; expire old secrets by time. Check: old secret rejected after the window

risks.description: [ssrf] Outbound HTTP client: A customer-supplied URL points at internal or metadata addresses.
risks.mitigation: Resolve and block private/link-local ranges; pin the resolved IP; forbid redirects to non-public hosts. Check: URL to 169.254.169.254 / 10.0.0.1 / localhost is refused before connecting

risks.description: [denial_of_service] Outbound HTTP client: A slow or infinite response body ties up a worker.
risks.mitigation: Per-request timeout; cap response size; stream and discard bodies. Check: target that stalls is cut at the timeout; 100 MB body is cut at the cap

risks.description: [information_disclosure] Outbound HTTP client: Secrets or internal headers leak to targets.
risks.mitigation: Send only the documented headers; never forward inbound headers. Check: captured request has exactly the documented headers

risks.description: [tampering] Signer: Signatures without a timestamp can be replayed.
risks.mitigation: Sign timestamp + body; document a tolerance window for verifiers. Check: replay outside the window fails verification

risks.description: [denial_of_service] Notifier: Notification storms and template injection.
risks.mitigation: Rate-limit per recipient; escape template context. Check: 1,000 failures produce one digest per owner

risks.description: [spoofing] Authentication: Credential stuffing or leaked keys.
risks.mitigation: Hash keys at rest; allow revocation; rate-limit failures. Check: revoked key is rejected within seconds; brute force is throttled

risks.description: [elevation] Authentication: A caller acts on another tenant's resources.
risks.mitigation: Every core operation takes the principal and checks ownership. Check: cross-tenant request returns 404/403 for every operation

risks.description: [spoofing] Admin HTTP API: Management operations reachable without authentication.
risks.mitigation: Authenticate in one middleware for every management route; deny by default. Check: every management route returns 401 unauthenticated

risks.description: [repudiation] Admin HTTP API: No record of who changed what.
risks.mitigation: Audit log entries for every management write with the principal. Check: each write produces an audit entry

risks.description: [elevation] Admin HTTP API: A customer manages another customer's resources.
risks.mitigation: Ownership check on every resource operation. Check: cross-customer access returns 404

risks.description: [spoofing] Ingest API: Any network peer can publish events.
risks.mitigation: Authenticate producers (service credentials); allowlist event types. Check: unauthenticated publish returns 401

risks.description: [tampering] Ingest API: Duplicate or replayed publishes create duplicate work.
risks.mitigation: Idempotency key per event; reject or de-duplicate replays. Check: replaying the same key does not enqueue twice

risks.description: [denial_of_service] Ingest API: A producer floods the ingest path.
risks.mitigation: Per-producer rate limit; back-pressure with 429 and Retry-After. Check: flood from one producer is throttled
